data.title: About Energy Innovation Centre
data.subtitle: Ganpat University — Centre of Excellence
data.description: Committed to philanthropic social upliftment, cutting-edge clean energy research, and India's transition to sustainable mobility.

body: In the era of increasing industrialization and urbanization, there is an increased demand for energy which is usually generated from fossil fuels. The use of fossil fuels leads to enhanced emissions of greenhouse gases, elevated pollution levels, and planet warming resulting in catastrophic climate change.

To save the planet, we must completely shift to renewable energy sources for our use in homes, offices, transport, and industries. Clean sources such as solar, wind, biomass, and biogas harness energy without harmful emissions, generating green power.

According to IPCC surveys, traffic accounts for 23% of worldwide CO2 emissions. Electric vehicles (EVs) counter this by operating with zero tailpipe emissions. At Ganpat University (GUNI), our Energy Innovation Centre is actively addressing EV challenges—including fast charging, high battery capacity, and life testing protocols—while integrating them into an intelligent campus microgrid.

data.title: Renewable Energy
data.subtitle: Sources of Naturally Replenished Power
data.description: Exploring solar, wind, biomass, and hydrogen technologies to eliminate reliance on fossil fuels.

body: Renewable energy is useful energy collected from renewable resources, which are naturally replenished on a human timescale, including sunlight, wind, rain, tides, waves, geothermal heat, and biomass.

At Ganpat University (GUNI), our Energy Innovation Centre is actively exploring and deploying multiple renewable generation avenues:
1. Solar Photovoltaic: Rooftop and ground-mounted solar arrays powering campus faculties and labs.
2. Wind Energy: Micro-turbines and hybrid solar-wind installations providing round-the-clock power.
3. Biomass & Biogas: Organic farm and cafeteria waste anaerobic digestion producing clean methane fuel.
4. Clean Storage Integration: Coupling renewable generation with battery energy storage systems (BESS) to smooth out generation intermittencies.

data.title: Electric Vehicles (EVs)
data.subtitle: Next-Generation Clean Mobility
data.description: Driving zero-emission transportation through advanced electric powertrains and smart battery packs.

body: An electric vehicle (EV) operates on an electric motor instead of an internal combustion engine (ICE). Unlike gasoline and diesel cars, EVs emit zero tailpipe CO2, reduce urban noise, and deliver significantly higher well-to-wheel energy efficiency.

Yet, EVs are truly carbon-neutral only if the batteries and electricity to power them come from renewable resources. To overcome current limitations—such as range anxiety, long charging times, and battery degradation—our centre focuses on developing superior fast-charging protocols, high-energy-density battery packs, robust motor controllers, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) emergency backup integration.

data.title: Microgrid Technology
data.subtitle: Self-Sufficient Smart Energy Systems
data.description: Creating intelligent distributed power systems that ensure 100% reliable, clean energy for our campus.

body: A microgrid is a self-sufficient energy system that serves a discrete geographic footprint—such as a university campus, hospital complex, or small township. It integrates multiple distributed energy resources (solar arrays, wind turbines, biogas plants, battery energy storage) and can operate either connected to the state electrical grid or in autonomous islanded mode.

Ganpat University is developing Project PRISM (Project for Research & Installation of Smart Microgrid) in collaboration with IIT Hyderabad and the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE). PRISM optimizes renewable power flows, enhances power quality, and provides frequency and voltage stabilization across campus substations.

data.title: Energy Storage & Conversion
data.subtitle: Advanced Batteries & Power Electronics
data.description: Mitigating renewable intermittency through novel electrode materials and high-efficiency converters.

body: Energy storage is essential for bridging the gap between intermittent renewable generation and real-time energy demand. When the sun sets or wind slows, stored energy guarantees uncompromised electrical supply.

Our research focuses on:
- Developing fast-charging, high-storage, and longer-lasting battery cells using novel anode/cathode materials.
- Standardizing testing protocols for battery life prediction and accelerated aging analysis.
- Designing high-efficiency bidirectional inverters and DC-DC converters for smooth power conversion and minimum dissipation.

data.title: Biogas Project
data.subtitle: Campus Organic Waste to Clean Energy
data.description: Transforming cafeteria food waste and agricultural biomass into clean green methane fuel.

body: The Biogas Project at Ganpat Vidyanagar is an exemplary circular economy initiative. By utilizing cattle manure (gobar), canteen food waste, and green farm biomass, the anaerobic digestion plant generates high-calorific methane for campus heating, cooking, and auxiliary power generation.

Key Parameters:
- Area: 50 Sq. Feet dedicated digestion area
- Depth: 10 Feet cylindrical digester tank
- Feedstocks: Gobar, cafeteria waste, and shredded agri-biomass
- Piping: High-pressure PVC pipeline with gas scrubbing and flow metering
- Byproduct: Nutrient-rich organic slurry utilized as bio-fertilizer on campus botanical farms.

data.title: Padmashri Ganpatbhai Patel
data.subtitle: Patron & President — Ganpat University
data.description: Pioneering sustainable technological innovation and research excellence at Ganpat University Energy Innovation Centre (EIC).

body: Padmashri Ganpatbhai Patel (Dada) is an industrialist, philanthropist, and the visionary founder of Ganpat University. His lifelong commitment to social upliftment through education has transformed a rural setting into Ganpat Vidyanagar—a world-class educational hub spanning over 300 acres.

Under his inspiring mentorship, the Energy Innovation Centre was conceived to establish clean energy self-sufficiency, model international collaborations with CalPoly Pomona, and spearhead green technology development for Gujarat and India.

data.description: Pioneering sustainable technological innovation and research excellence at Ganpat University Energy Innovation Centre (EIC).

body: Dr. Mahendra Sharma is the Pro-Chancellor and Director General of Ganpat University. With a doctorate in Consumer Behaviour, Dr. Sharma possesses extensive expertise in strategic management, institutional growth, and global academic partnerships.

He has pioneered industry-aligned programs with IBM, Oracle, and SAP, and has led international agreements with Victoria University (Australia) and Penn State University (USA). Under his leadership, the Energy Innovation Centre is executing high-impact research proposals with MNRE and IIT Hyderabad.
